item.title: Amakusa Islands — Guide
item.description: The Amakusa Islands, a beautiful chain of over a hundred islands off the west coast of Kumamoto, combine gorgeous coastal scenery with fascinating history and abundant wildlife. Connected to the mainland and each other by a series of bridges (the ‘Amakusa Five Bridges’) and ferries, they are one of the best places in Japan for wild dolphin watching, with resident pods of bottlenose dolphins seen year-round on boat tours. Amakusa also has a poignant Christian history: it was a stronghold of persecuted ‘hidden Christians’ and the centre of the 1637 Shimabara-Amakusa Rebellion, and its churches and related sites form part of a UNESCO World Heritage listing.

item.title: Yakushima Whale & Dolphin Watching — Guide
item.description: The warm seas off Yakushima and southern Kagoshima are a rewarding spot for whale and dolphin watching. From roughly January to April, humpback whales migrate through these waters, and boat tours head out for the thrilling chance to see these giant creatures breaching, spouting and diving in the open sea — an unforgettable wildlife spectacle. Pods of dolphins are also frequently encountered year-round, often riding the bow waves of the boats and delighting passengers with their acrobatics.

item.title: Choshi Whale & Dolphin Watching Guide: Tours & Access
item.description: Few people realise you can go whale and dolphin watching within easy reach of Tokyo — but the rich waters off Choshi, where the warm Kuroshio current meets the cold Oyashio off the Boso Peninsula’s northeastern tip, are one of Japan’s most reliable spots. Boat tours head out from Choshi port to look for large pods of dolphins (often hundreds at a time) and, in season, whales such as minke, Bryde’s and even sperm whales.

item.title: Enoshima Aquarium Guide: Tickets, Highlights & Access
item.description: Right on the Shonan coast facing Enoshima island, the Enoshima Aquarium — affectionately known as “Enosui” — is one of the Tokyo area’s most beloved aquariums, blending marine science with a stunning seaside setting.
